maria: Quick sketch: propose a small prefix WAL (per-tenant/prefix) for staged cache deltas so evict+restart don't lose ordering.
aj: What exactly fails today?
maria: Chaos test: in-flight cache-only deltas were applied out-of-order after eviction; restart caused stale cursor reads until background rehydrate finished.
kevin: WAL seems sensible. Where does it live? local SSD vs shared blob store?
soph: Local SSD = low latency but handoff trouble; shared store = replayable but higher tail.
dave: Idea: piggyback seq allocation on prefix lease-holder. Lease-holder writes WAL entries and acks after durable write. Others proxy. Keeps ordering local.
aj: Handoff rule: owner must checkpoint and publish last_seq before transfer; new owner loads checkpoint then replays entries > last_seq.
kevin: Ack semantics must be strict: ack only after durable write. Maybe a weak-ack opt-in for non-critical deltas.
soph: GC: truncate WAL after checkpoint; snapshot frequency tradeoff vs disk usage.
dave: Metrics: WAL_write_p95, backlog_per_prefix, checkpoint_time, replay_time. Chaos tests for kill/restart, partitioning.
ops-bot: Ops note: avoid co-locating multiple heavy WAL owners on same rack during canary.
maria: Rollout plan: Phase 0 instrumentation -> Phase 1 local-durable WAL + no handoff while dirty -> Phase 2 shared-replay + checkpointing -> Phase 3 perf tuning. I'll open a doc/PR. Please comment on failure modes and KMS/encryption needs.
aj: Will review ordering/edge cases.
kevin: I'll add KMS/encryption notes.
soph: I'll run perf sims for write amplification.
dave: I'll list chaos tests.
maria: Thanks, closing for now.
